question: Should immutable action-ledger publishing retain enough bounded retries to cover the documented sustained contention, or is failing after the new additive budget an accepted delivery contract?
rationale: The patch intentionally trades multiplicative retries for a lower fixed ceiling, but the supplied production evidence exceeded that ceiling; choosing acceptable reliability versus bounded execution time is a maintainer policy decision.

options.title: Preserve bounded delivery capacity
options.body: Keep the flattened non-nested algorithm but derive a bounded budget that covers the observed contention and add a higher-race real-Git regression test.

options.title: Accept early failure semantics
options.body: Keep the 12-push budget only if maintainers explicitly accept that an immutable ledger publish may fail under sustained writers and document the subsequent recovery path.

options.title: Pause for contention policy
options.body: Defer this PR until the repair lane has an explicit end-to-end retry and recovery contract for continuous state-branch contention.

recommendation.title: Preserve bounded delivery capacity
recommendation.body: Keep the flattened non-nested algorithm but derive a bounded budget that covers the observed contention and add a higher-race real-Git regression test.

likelyOwner.reason: The available PR evidence identifies this contributor as the person most familiar with the affected retry path and production contention scenario.
